data.description:
# Intake Brief: Untracked skill dir from a concurrent agent breaks the full-suite collection for all agents

**Work item:** SA-0MUPDDMXB0088CMM (bug, critical)

## Problem statement

When a concurrent agent leaves an **untracked** `skill/<new-skill>/` directory
in the main checkout mid-session, the full test suite fails from the repo root
for **every** agent: the new skill's `tests/` package collides with the
top-level `tests` package (`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named
'tests.<name>'`), and the skill-hygiene tests discover the unwired
`SKILL.md`. The pre-push full-suite gate therefore false-fails while another
agent's work-in-progress is present — the multi-agent testing deadlock class
tracked by SA-0MTG0Y34T007ZHPF.

## Users

- **Agents working in the shared main checkout** — they must run the
  pre-push full suite and currently cannot while another agent has untracked
  skill WIP, forcing `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` bypasses or manual coordination.
  - As an agent in the main checkout, I want `pytest` from the repo root to
    pass (or report an actionable warning) even when another agent's untracked
    skill directory is present, so my pre-push gate is not blocked by WIP I do
    not own.
  - As a reviewer, I want real regressions not to be masked by a collection
    `ImportError` caused by unrelated untracked files, so failures remain
    trustworthy.
- **The producer/operator** — wants deterministic, low-noise test gating
  across concurrent agents.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. An untracked `skill/<new-skill>/` directory in the main checkout no longer
   breaks `pytest` collection from the repo root (its colliding `tests/`
   package is excluded rather than raising `ModuleNotFoundError`).
2. The skill inventory / hygiene checks ignore untracked (unwired) skill
   directories and surface a clear, actionable "untracked skill dir present"
   warning naming the ignored directory/directories, rather than a confusing
   `ImportError`.
3. Tracked skill directories are still collected and validated normally —
   the filter must not silently skip real skills.
4. Regression tests reproduce the untracked-directory scenario (collection
   isolation, warning emission, and inventory filtering) and fail without the
   fix.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Must work from the **main checkout**, where concurrent agents may create
  untracked skill directories; worktrees must remain unaffected.
- No test-collection option may weaken coverage of **tracked** skills — the
  filter is scoped strictly to git-untracked `skill/<name>/` directories.
- Must not depend on operators remembering to clean up other agents' WIP.
- Resolution keyed to git tracking status (portable, no reliance on
  `.gitignore` entries that other agents may not have).

## Existing state

- A concurrent agent's untracked `skill/machine-hygiene/` directory triggered
  the failure (it has since been committed, but the defect class is generic to
  any untracked `skill/<new-skill>/`).
- The repo-root `conftest.py` previously only armed the live-repo mutation
  guard (SA-0MUG30JSE0069JEQ); it had no untracked-skill handling.
- The implementation for this work item has **already landed on local `dev`**
  (commits `9aea9207` and `8d3e1d28`) from a prior session:
  - `conftest.py` now hooks `pytest_ignore_collect` to skip untracked
    `skill/<name>/` directories, caches the git-tracked check, and emits a
    one-time actionable warning at `pytest_configure`.
  - `skill/context-audit/scripts/measure_context.py` gains
    `tracked_skill_dirs()` / `untracked_skill_dirs()`; `skill_description_prose()`
    and `hidden_skill_names()` ignore untracked dirs.
  - `tests/test_report_wiring_hygiene.py` filters to tracked skills and warns.
  - Regression coverage in `tests/test_untracked_skill_directory_isolation.py`
    (7 tests; verified passing: `7 passed in 1.66s`).
- The two implementation commits are ahead of `origin/dev` (not yet pushed).

## Desired change

Make the repo-root test suite resilient to a concurrent agent's untracked
skill directory by excluding git-untracked `skill/<name>/` trees from pytest
collection and from the skill inventory, while emitting a clear warning that
names the ignored directory/directories. Preserve normal collection and
validation of tracked skills. Document the behaviour in the root `conftest.py`
and the centralised inventory helper.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `conftest.py` — `pytest_ignore_collect` hook filtering untracked
  `skill/<name>/` dirs; cached git-tracked check; actionable warning at
  `pytest_configure`.
- `skill/context-audit/scripts/measure_context.py` — single-source-of-truth
  `tracked_skill_dirs()` / `untracked_skill_dirs()`; untracked-aware
  `skill_description_prose()` and `hidden_skill_names()`.
- `tests/test_untracked_skill_directory_isolation.py` — regression coverage for
  collection isolation, warning emission, and inventory filtering.
- `tests/test_report_wiring_hygiene.py` — tracked-skill filter + warning.

## Related work

### Related work items

- **SA-0MTG0Y34T007ZHPF** — *(feature, high, in-progress)* "When multiple
  agents are working they can become blocked on audits/testing" — the parent
  multi-agent testing deadlock class this defect belongs to.
- **SA-0MUG30JSE0069JEQ** — *(task, high, completed)* Repo-root conftest
  live-repo guard — the same `conftest.py` surface this change extends.
- **SA-0MS1T7A5W003UJUH** — Remove `skill/ralph/` directory tree (completed).
- **SA-0MRMCK0C8008ESE0** — [test-failure] `test_audit_skill_doc.py` failing
  test (completed).
- **SA-0ML8XKRV80GORAL7** — Fix scheduler `wl stats` command (completed).

### Related repository artefacts

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk (scope creep):** broadening the filter to "any untracked file" could
  mask legitimate new tests; the fix is deliberately scoped to untracked
  `skill/<name>/` directories, and tracked skills remain validated normally.
- **Risk:** a partially-added skill (tracked directory, untracked files) is
  not covered — if observed, raise a follow-up work item rather than widening
  scope here.
- **Assumption:** git tracking status is the correct discriminator between
  another agent's WIP and committed work; verified by the regression tests.
- **Assumption:** a warning (not a hard failure) is the desired behaviour while
  WIP is present, per AC2.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required: the seed context already specified the
problem, impact, and testable acceptance criteria, and repository/git-history
inspection supplied the remaining evidence (root `conftest.py` state,
`measure_context` inventory helper, existing regression test, and the landed
commits `9aea9207` / `8d3e1d28`).

Intake brief completed (Map).

Five mini-reviews:
1. Completeness: no changes needed \u2014 problem, users, ACs, constraints present.
2. Capture fidelity: no changes needed \u2014 seed context represented faithfully.
3. Related-work & traceability: preserved the automated find-related report (3 related items, 3 repo matches); linked SA-0MTG0Y34T007ZHPF (deadlock class) and SA-0MUG30JSE0069JEQ (conftest surface).
4. Risks & assumptions: added scope-creep risk (filter deliberately limited to untracked skill dirs) and part-tracked-dir follow-up guidance.
5. Polish & handoff: tightened language; recorded the already-landed fix (commits 9aea9207, 8d3e1d28) as Existing state; regression tests verified (7 passed).

Issue type corrected task -> bug (broken-suite defect, matching triage convention). AC coverage review: proceed. Effort: Small (~11.8h recommended); Risk: Medium.
